title: प्रभावकारी शिक्षणः नेपाली शिक्षामा अध्ययनरत विद्यार्थीका विचार {Effective Teaching: Students' views on Nepali Education}
nepali: यस लेखमा कस्तो शिक्षण भयो भने नेपाली शिक्षा विषयका विद्यार्थीमा रुचि बढाउन सकिन्छ र उनीहरूले अपेक्षित सिकाइउपलब्धि हासिल गर्दछन् भन्ने प्रश्नको जवाफ खोजिएको छ। विद्यार्थीहरू के चाहन्छन्, उनीहरूको विचारमा शिक्षकले कस्तो विधि र प्रक्रिया अपनाउँदा शिक्षण उपलब्धिमूलक हुन्छ भन्ने बारेमा उनीहरूलाई नै सोधेर, उनीहरूका विचारपहिचान गरी उनीहरूकै अनुभवका आधारमा प्रभावकारी शिक्षणका उपायहरू खोजी गर्न‘ यस लेखको मूल उद्देश्य रहेको छ । यहाँ गुणात्मक अनुसन्धानको घटना प्रतिक्रिया अध्य (फेनोमेनोलोजी) विधिको प्रयोग गरी अन्तर्वार्ताका माध्यमबाट सूचना सङ्कलन गरिएको छ । सहभागीहरूबाट आएका सूचनालाई छोटा–छोटा बुँदा बनाई (कोडिङ गरी त्यसलाई समूह विभाजनगरेर मुख्य शीर्षकमा पुगी विश्लेषण गरिएको छ यस अनुसन्धानले शिक्षकमा पर्याप्त विषयवस्तुको ज्ञान हुनुपर्ने, अन्तरक्रियात्मक कक्षामा विद्यार्थीको रुचि बढ्ने, अध्यापन गर्दा एकोहोरो विषयवस्तुका बारेमा मात्र बताउनु भन्दा समसामयिक, व्यावहारिक, तात्कालिक र स्थानीय प्रसङ्गका कुराहरू जोडेर विद्यार्थीमा अभिरुचि जगाउनु उपयुक्त हुन्छ भन्ने निष्कर्ष निकालेको छ यसका साथै शिक्षकले बेला–बेलामा आफ्नो शिक्षण क्रियाकलापको बारेमा पृष्ठपोषण लिंदै सुधारात्मक शिक्षण गर्न‘ पर्ने जस्ता महत्त्वपूर्ण कुराहरू सहभागीको तर्फबाट आएका छन् त्यसैले यस लेखले शिक्षण कार्यमा संलग्न शिक्षकहरूका साथै सरोकारवालाहरू सबैलाई सहयोग पुग्न सक्छ भन्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ l
american_english: This article seeks an answer to the question of what kind of teaching would increase interest among students of Nepali Education and enable them to achieve the expected learning outcomes. The main objective of this article is to seek measures for effective teaching on the basis of the students' own experience, by asking the students themselves what they want and identifying their views on what methods and processes a teacher should adopt for teaching to be productive. Here, information has been collected through interviews using the phenomenological method of qualitative research. The information coming from the participants has been made into short points (coded), grouped and analyzed under main headings. This research has drawn the conclusion that the teacher should have adequate knowledge of the subject matter, that students' interest increases in interactive classes, and that rather than talking only about one-sided subject matter while teaching, it is appropriate to arouse students' interest by connecting contemporary, practical, immediate and local contextual matters. In addition, important matters have come from the participants' side, such as the teacher taking feedback on his or her teaching activities from time to time and conducting corrective teaching. Therefore, it is expected that this article may be of help to all teachers engaged in teaching work as well as to all stakeholders.

australian_english: This article looks for an answer to the question of what kind of teaching would boost interest among students of Nepali Education and let them achieve the expected learning outcomes. The main objective of this article is to seek ways to make teaching effective on the basis of the students' own experience, by asking the students themselves what they want and working out their views on what methods and processes a teacher should adopt for teaching to be productive. Here, information has been gathered through interviews using the phenomenological method of qualitative research. The information coming from the participants has been turned into short points (coded), grouped and analysed under main headings. This research has drawn the conclusion that the teacher should have adequate knowledge of the subject matter, that students' interest increases in interactive classes, and that rather than talking only about one-sided subject matter while teaching, it is appropriate to arouse students' interest by connecting contemporary, practical, immediate and local contextual matters. On top of that, important matters have come from the participants' side, such as the teacher taking feedback on his or her teaching activities from time to time and conducting corrective teaching. So it is expected that this article may be of help to all teachers engaged in teaching work as well as to all stakeholders.
informal_english: This article tries to answer: what kind of teaching gets Nepali Education students interested and helps them hit the expected learning outcomes? The main aim is to find ways to teach effectively, based on the students' own experience — asking them what they want, figuring out what methods and processes they reckon make teaching productive, and building on that. Here the info was gathered through interviews using a phenomenological approach to qualitative research. The stuff coming from participants was broken into short points (coded), grouped and analysed under main headings. The research concluded that teachers need solid subject knowledge, that students get more interested in interactive classes, and that rather than banging on about one-sided subject matter, it's better to spark students' interest by tying in contemporary, practical, immediate and local context. On top of that, participants raised important points like teachers getting feedback on their teaching now and then and doing corrective teaching. So the hope is this article helps all the teachers involved in teaching, plus everyone else with a stake in it.
